title: Terahertz-Driven Conformational Remodeling of Filamentous Actin: Insights into Intense Terahertz-Field-Mediated Biopolymer Responses.
authors: Liu, Chang; Zhang, Baolong; Shi, Chaojing; Liao, Guoqian; Wei, Yanyu; Ma, Jinglong; Ma, Ziyang; Zhu, Jiangrui; Li, Zhaoyu; Gao, Chutong; Zhang, Yaqun; Fu, Rao; Huang, Xiaorui; Liu, Ying; Qi, Feng; Ye, Fangfu; Guo, QianJin; Chen, Jianing; Wu, Xiaojun; Li, Ming; Fang, Weihai; Li, Yutong; Li, Yunliang
journal: The journal of physical chemistry letters
one_liner_zh: 该研究利用太赫兹脉冲调控肌动蛋白丝构象，结合光谱实验与机器学习分析，虽涉及蛋白质构象变化但缺乏结构计算建模或AI/物理模拟方法，对蛋白质结构计算课题启发有限。
abstract: We demonstrate the precise, noninvasive control of filamentous actin (F-actin) conformations using high-intensity terahertz (THz) pulses via a dominantly nonthermal mechanism. By combining femtosecond time-resolved mid-infrared spectroscopy, Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, super-resolution confocal imaging, and a data-driven machine learning pipeline (CNN-UMAP-K-means), we show that 0.4 THz pulses selectively weaken intermolecular beta-sheet structures (1615 cm-1) while enhancing alpha-helical content (1650 cm-1) in F-actin, driving a dynamical shift toward monomer-like (G-actin) vibrational energy relaxation (VER) with up to 95% spectral similarity. In A549 cells, THz irradiation systematically reduces F-actin aggregation, as evidenced by fluorescence imaging. The spectral and dynamical changes induced by THz differ distinctly from thermal denaturation, with no characteristic peak shift observed under heating, supporting a dominantly nonthermal mechanism; our observations are consistent with coupling between intense terahertz fields and collective low-frequency intermonomer vibrational motions within F-actin filaments. The machine learning framework enables unbiased clustering and quantitative similarity analysis to identify optimal irradiation parameters (70 muJ, 10 min) that maximize selective F-actin remodeling without perturbing G-actin integrity. This work establishes intense THz as a powerful photonic tool for manipulating protein assemblies at molecular and cellular levels, advancing our fundamental understanding of THz-biopolymer interactions for biophotonic applications.
abstract_zh: 我们展示了利用高强度太赫兹（THz）脉冲，通过主要非热机制，对丝状肌动蛋白（F-actin）构象进行精确、非侵入性控制。结合飞秒时间分辨中红外光谱、傅里叶变换红外（FTIR）光谱、超分辨共聚焦成像以及数据驱动的机器学习流程（CNN-UMAP-K-means），我们表明0.4 THz脉冲选择性削弱F-actin中的分子间β-折叠结构（1615 cm⁻¹），同时增强α-螺旋含量（1650 cm⁻¹），推动其向类单体（G-actin）振动能量弛豫（VER）的动态转变，光谱相似度高达95%。在A549细胞中，THz照射系统性减少F-actin聚集，荧光成像证实了这一点。THz诱导的光谱和动态变化与热变性明显不同，加热下未观察到特征峰位移，支持主要非热机制；我们的观察与强太赫兹场与F-actin丝内集体低频单体间振动模式之间的耦合一致。机器学习框架实现了无偏聚类和定量相似性分析，以确定最佳照射参数（70 μJ，10分钟），从而在不干扰G-actin完整性的情况下最大化选择性F-actin重塑。这项工作确立了强THz作为在分子和细胞水平操纵蛋白质组装的有力光子工具，推进了我们对THz-生物聚合物相互作用的基础理解，为生物光子应用奠定基础。
